name: Beta-sarcoglycan-related limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R4

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus diagnostic criteria for limb-girdle muscular dystrophies

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting pelvic and shoulder girdles
Muscle biopsy showing dystrophic changes with reduced or absent beta-sarcoglycan protein expression on immunohistochemistry
Identification of pathogenic variants in the SGCB gene
Elevated serum creatine kinase levels (typically 5-50 times upper limit of normal)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness with either muscle biopsy showing reduced beta-sarcoglycan or identification of pathogenic SGCB variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is considered gold standard; muscle biopsy remains important when genetic testing is inconclusive.

common.symptomName: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated liver enzymes
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective fatty replacement and muscle atrophy in proximal limb muscles
Cardiac MRI may show mild cardiomyopathy
other: Muscle biopsy with dystrophic changes and absent or reduced beta-sarcoglycan staining

distinguishingFeatures: Calpainopathy (LGMD R1) typically shows calpain-3 deficiency on muscle biopsy
Different genetic mutations in CAPN3 gene
Dysferlinopathy (LGMD R2) presents with distal muscle involvement and absent dysferlin protein

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory failure
Marked elevation of serum creatine kinase >50 times normal
references: Orphanet: Beta-sarcoglycan-related limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R4 (ORPHA:119)
Nigro V, Savarese M. Genetic basis of limb-girdle muscular dystrophies: the 2022 update. Acta Myol. 2022
Bushby K, et al. Diagnosis and management of limb-girdle muscular dystrophies: consensus recommendations. Neurology. 2014
